![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/001019dd20e7a56980201a07e94d3fb9e7824bdeef6864c90abb3172babce734.png)

The scatter plot above shows the time (in minutes) it takes some professional cyclists to cover particular distances during training. 
Use the trend line to estimate how long it takes one of these cyclists to travel $4$ miles.
feedback.worked_solution:
To make our estimation, we proceed as follows:

- We start at $y=4$ on the vertical axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/19cf6fe36f3afb0322e51ab1d9b1d580453380ba67d813a923818756c1d57994.png)

- Then, we move right until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/8815a1433c0c139ecf9370da8a6799b084a0e875a3bddb1b80ffa96792c9a145.png)

- Finally, we move down until we intersect the horizontal axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/f183ff82c15c750d47a0da10151917c02311260f0e86daecfeb1b12c9e15007c.png)

Therefore, these cyclists travel $4$ miles in approximately $20$ minutes.
